record.paper_title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces
record.original_question: Suppose K is an adequate full subcategory of Top0 that is closed under homeomorphisms. Does the K-reflection functor preserve arbitrary products of T0 spaces; equivalently, for every family {X_i}, is the K-reflection of prod_i X_i homeomorphic to prod_i X_i^K?

evidence.quote: Question 7.14. ([49]) Suppose that K is adequate and closed with respect to homeomorphisms. Does the K-reflection functor preserves arbitrary products of T0 spaces?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbf{Top}_0$ denote the category of $T_0$ topological spaces with continuous maps. A full subcategory $\mathbf{K}$ of $\mathbf{Top}_0$ is called a reflective subcategory if the inclusion functor has a left adjoint, called the $\mathbf{K}$-reflection; for each $T_0$ space $X$, this yields a space $X^{\mathbf{K}} \in \mathbf{K}$ and a continuous map $\eta_X : X \to X^{\mathbf{K}}$ universal among continuous maps from $X$ to objects of $\mathbf{K}$. 

For a $T_0$ space $X$, let $\mathcal{H}(X)$ denote the irreducible-closed-subsets approach: equip the set of nonempty closed subsets of $X$ with the lower Vietoris-type topology generated by $\{A \subseteq X : A \cap U \neq \emptyset\}$ for $U$ open in $X$, and let $P_H(X)$ denote the resulting space (the Smyth/Hoare-type hyperspace as used for K-reflections). Call $\mathbf{K}$ adequate if $\mathbf{K}$ is a full subcategory of $\mathbf{Top}_0$ closed under homeomorphisms such that for every $T_0$ space $X$, the canonical subspace $P_H(\mathbf{K}(X))$ associated with the $\mathbf{K}$-reflection construction is itself an object of $\mathbf{K}$ (so that the standard construction produces a reflection). Examples of adequate categories include the categories of sober spaces, $d$-spaces, well-filtered spaces, and the Keimel–Lawson category.

Question: Suppose $\mathbf{K}$ is an adequate full subcategory of $\mathbf{Top}_0$ that is closed under homeomorphisms. Does the $\mathbf{K}$-reflection functor preserve arbitrary products of $T_0$ spaces? Equivalently, for every family $\{X_i\}_{i \in I}$ of $T_0$ spaces, is the canonical continuous map
$$\Big(\prod_{i \in I} X_i\Big)^{\mathbf{K}} \longrightarrow \prod_{i \in I} X_i^{\mathbf{K}}$$
a homeomorphism?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in the study of K-reflections of T0 spaces. Existing work (e.g., the direct approach to K-reflections by Xu, arXiv:1911.11618) establishes that adequate K-reflections preserve finite products of T0 spaces, but preservation of arbitrary products remains unresolved in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: A direct approach to K-reflections of T0 spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Provides a direct construction of K-reflections for adequate subcategories K of Top0 and discusses preservation properties, with finite-product preservation established.
status_evidence.claim: Finite product preservation is established for adequate K; arbitrary product case is not resolved.
